name: TPS26632RGER
title: TPS2663x: 60 V, 6 A industrial eFuse with power limiting, surge protection and blocking-FET driver
summary: A family of 60 V, 6 A electronic fuses built round a 31 mΩ integrated hot-swap FET, for 4.5 V to 60 V industrial rails (67 V absolute maximum). A driver for an external N-channel FET adds input reverse-polarity protection down to -60 V and fast reverse-current blocking. Resistors set the current limit (0.6 A to 6 A), UVLO, the overvoltage cut-off (TPS26630, TPS26631) and, on the PLIM variants, an output power limit; the other variants clamp overvoltage at a fixed level; a capacitor sets the output slew rate. Outputs are a fault flag, a power-good signal with its own threshold input, and an analog current monitor. TPS26632RGER is the 24-pin VQFN part with a fixed 35 V maximum overvoltage clamp, 1x current limiting and adjustable output power limiting.

pins.name: DRV

pins.name: IN_SYS

pins.name: UVLO
pins.function: Undervoltage lockout input. Below its threshold the FET turns off and FLT goes low. Tied to GND it selects the internal 15 V lockout on IN_SYS; tied to IN_SYS it disables the function. Must not float.

pins.name: OVP
pins.function: Overvoltage input (TPS26630, TPS26631). Above its threshold the FET turns off and FLT goes low. Tied to GND it selects the internal 34.3 V cut-off.

pins.name: PLIM
pins.function: Output power limit input (TPS26632, TPS26633, TPS26635, TPS26636, TPS26637). A resistor to GND sets the power limit; tied to GND the power limit is off.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground of the device; goes to system ground.

pins.name: dVdT
pins.function: Slew-rate control: a capacitor to GND fixes how fast the output rises at turn-on.

pins.name: ILIM
pins.function: Current-limit setting: a resistor to GND fixes the overload limit, and with it the fast-trip level. A short or an open on this pin keeps the FET off.

pins.name: MODE
pins.function: Selects the response to an overload fault: open for latch-off, shorted to GND for auto-retry.

pins.name: SHDN
pins.function: Active-low shutdown input. Low puts the device into low-current shutdown; toggling it clears a latched fault. Open-circuit level about 2.7 V.

pins.name: IMON
pins.function: Current monitor output: a current proportional to the FET current, turned into a voltage by a resistor to GND. Unconnected when unused.

pins.name: FLT
pins.function: Active-low open-drain fault output. Unused, it may float or be tied to GND.

pins.name: PGTH

pins.name: PGOOD

circuits.title: 24 V, 2 A input protection for an industrial PLC or CNC CPU
circuits.description: A TPS26630 or TPS26631 guards the 24 V input of a PLC controller and feeds a DC-DC converter. Q1 (CSD19537Q3) is the back-to-back blocking FET for reverse polarity and reverse current, and Q2 (BSS138) pulls Q1's gate down quickly. D1 (SMCJ36CA) clamps surge at the input and CIN is 1 µF. R1, R2, R3 (887 k, 29.4 k, 34 k) set an 18 V undervoltage lockout and a 33 V overvoltage cut-off. RILIM = 9.09 k gives a 2 A current limit; CdVdT = 100 nF holds inrush near 500 mA into the 1 mF output capacitor. R4/R5 (499 k/56 k) put the power-good threshold at the converter's 12 V lockout, and PGOOD with a 24 k pull-up enables the converter. MODE is grounded for auto-retry.

parts.note: bidirectional TVS; pins 1 to the input rail, 2 to GND

circuits.title: Typical application, TPS26632, TPS26633, TPS26635, TPS26636 and TPS26637
circuits.description: The power-limiting variants on a 4.5 V to 60 V rail. Q1 and Q2 are the optional blocking FET and its gate pull-down, needed only for reverse-current blocking and reverse-polarity protection. R1/R2 set the UVLO level, R3 from PLIM to GND sets the output power limit, RILIM the current limit and CdVdT the output slew rate. R4/R5 from OUT set the power-good threshold. RIMON turns the IMON current into a voltage for a load monitor. PGOOD and FLT are outputs and SHDN is the on/off control.
notes: MODE is left open, which selects latch-off.

circuits.title: Simplified schematic, TPS26630 and TPS26631
circuits.description: The adjustable-OVP variants on a 4.5 V to 60 V rail. D1 is a TVS fitted only for surge suppression; Q1 and Q2 are the optional blocking FET and gate pull-down for reverse-current blocking and reverse-polarity protection. R1, R2 and R3 form one divider from IN_SYS that sets both the UVLO and OVP levels. RILIM sets the current limit, CdVdT the slew rate, R4/R5 the power-good threshold, and RILON loads IMON for a load monitor.

parts.note: TVS for surge suppression only; pins 1 to the input rail, 2 to GND

notes: MODE is left open, which selects latch-off.

circuits.title: TPS26630 as a simple 24 V supply path protector
circuits.description: The fewest parts: blocking FET Q1, gate pull-down Q2, RILIM, CIN and COUT. UVLO and OVP are grounded, so the internal 15 V lockout and 34 V overvoltage cut-off apply; MODE is grounded for auto-retry; dVdT is open for the fastest start; PGTH is tied to OUT. With these connections the circuit gives reverse-polarity protection to -60 V with a 60 V rated Q1, reverse-current blocking, a 24 V/240 µs output slew rate and current limiting.

circuits.title: Priority power mux with two TPS26630
circuits.description: Two TPS26630 share one output. U1 passes the main input VIN_MAIN and U2 the auxiliary input VIN_AUX, each behind its own blocking FET (Q1, Q3) and gate pull-down (Q2, Q4). U1's dVdT node drives the gate of Q5, which links U2's IN to U2's OVP pin above R8: while the main channel is on, U2's OVP is pulled high and the auxiliary channel stays off. When the main input drops below the level set by R1-R3, U1 turns off, Q5 releases and U2 takes over the output. One divider R4/R5 on the output feeds both PGTH pins. Each channel has its own current-limit, slew-rate and current-monitor parts.

parts.note: switches U2's OVP from U1's dVdT

notes: Changeover happens in about tOVP(fast_dly); the output droop during it is given by the droop equation.

circuits.title: Optional transient protection parts
circuits.description: The basic circuit with the parts that absorb transients: a bidirectional TVS (D1) and a ceramic capacitor (CIN) at the input, and a Schottky diode (D2) from the output to GND for negative spikes. The blocking FET pair Q1/Q2, the R1-R3 divider for UVLO and OVP, RILIM and CdVdT are as in the other circuits; R4 alone ties PGTH to OUT.

parts.note: optional bidirectional TVS; pins 1 to the input rail, 2 to GND

notes: TVS, input capacitor and Schottky are optional.

operation.text: TPS26630 and TPS26631 have an adjustable overvoltage cut-off on the OVP pin. TPS26632 and TPS26633 clamp the output at a fixed 35 V maximum, TPS26635 and TPS26636 at 39 V maximum; TPS26637 has no overvoltage function. All but TPS26630 and TPS26631 add adjustable output power limiting on PLIM. TPS26631, TPS26633, TPS26635 and TPS26637 allow a 2x pulse of overload current; the others limit at 1x.

A capacitor from dVdT to GND sets the output rise rate at turn-on; with dVdT open the output rises at the fastest rate, about 24 V in 500 µs. The output voltage follows 25 times the dVdT voltage, which is charged by 2 µA.

When large output capacitance would push the FET past its safe power-versus-time curve, a loop holds the junction at T(J_REG), 145 °C typical, by reducing the charging current. A timer, t(Treg_timeout), starts with regulation; if the output has not come up by then, the FET turns off and MODE decides between retry and latch-off. The loop is active during start-up from V(IN), after UVLO cycling and after SHDN turn-on, and switches off once the FET is fully enhanced or the timer expires.

PGOOD is open drain and rated to 60 V; it may be pulled up to IN_SYS or OUT. It goes high when the FET is enhanced and PGTH is above V(PGTHR), with a rising deglitch of tPGOODR, and low when PGTH falls below V(PGTHF), after tPGOODF. It can enable a downstream converter.

On recovery from a fault (OVP going low, UVLO going high) the device samples PGTH. If PGTH is still above V(PGTHF), the output is taken to be a system transient: the FET turns on fast, after the fast turn-on delay, ignoring the dVdT capacitor, with thermal regulation active for tCL_PLIM(dly), and current limited at I(OL) (TPS26630, TPS26632) or 2 × I(OL) (the others) for up to tCB(dly). If PGTH is below V(PGTHF), the FET ramps in dVdT mode with the limit at I(OL). Tying PGTH to GND disables fast recovery and holds PGOOD low.

The UVLO comparator is ±2 % accurate with 78 mV typical hysteresis; below V(UVLOF) the FET turns off quickly and FLT goes low. A divider from the supply to UVLO sets the level. UVLO tied to GND selects the internal 15 V lockout on IN_SYS, with 1 V hysteresis. Tied to IN_SYS, the lockout is disabled; it must not float. Where reverse polarity protection is needed, at least 300 kΩ goes between UVLO and IN_SYS.

TPS26630 and TPS26631 turn the FET off when OVP exceeds V(OVPR) (±2 %); a divider from IN_SYS sets the level, and OVP tied to GND selects the internal 34.3 V cut-off with 440 mV hysteresis. The clamp variants hold the output at V(OVC) once the input passes the clamp level; the FET then dissipates (V(IN_SYS) – V(OVC)) × I(OUT). The clamp lasts at most tOVC(dly), 162 ms typical, before the FET turns off and MODE decides what follows. FLT goes low 617 µs typical after entering the clamp and stays low until the overvoltage clears.

An external N-channel FET Q1 with source at IN_SYS, drain at IN and gate at B_GATE forms a back-to-back pair with the internal FET and blocks reverse input. A signal FET Q2 with gate at DRV, drain at B_GATE and source at IN_SYS pulls Q1's gate down fast in reverse-current and reverse-polarity events. B_GATE drives 10.2 V typical. IN_SYS – OUT may reach -85 V, a stress that appears across Q1 during surge. Q2 needs at least 15 V VDS, a 20 V maximum VGS, Ciss ≤ 50 pF and VGTH(min) ≤ 3 V. Without the external FETs, IN_SYS and IN are joined and B_GATE and DRV stay open.

The device compares V(IN_SYS) with V(OUT). When the difference falls below -1 V, Q1 is turned off in tRCB(fast_dly) plus the driver delay. For smaller overdrive the turn-off is slower, which gives immunity to supply noise. After an input hot short, Q1 turns back on about 1.6 ms typical once the forward difference V(IN_SYS) – V(OUT) passes about 67 mV.

Load current is sensed across an internal resistor during start-up and normal running. On TPS26630 and TPS26632 an overload is regulated at I(OL), the output voltage falling as needed, for at most tCL_PLIM(dly), 162 ms typical, unless thermal shutdown comes first; MODE then decides retry or latch-off. On the 2x variants, once PGOOD is high, an overload above I(OL) starts a tCB(dly) timer (25.5 ms typical) during which up to 2 × I(OL) is passed; after it the limit drops to I(OL) for at most tCL_PLIM(dly). With PGOOD low, as during start-up or retry, only I(OL) is allowed. A short or open on ILIM keeps the FET off until it is removed.

A fast-trip comparator turns the FET off within 1 µs typical at I(SCP) = 45 A, faster than the current-limit loop can act. The threshold is I(FASTTRIP); after a few microseconds off, the FET turns back on slowly and the current-limit loop regulates at I(OL). Between I(FASTTRIP) and I(SCP) the response is 3.2 µs typical. Starting into a short, the current limits at I(OL), thermal regulation holds the junction at T(J_REG) for t(Treg_timeout), and FLT goes low after that timeout and stays low until the short is gone.

With a fixed current limit, the available output power rises with the supply; the PLIM variants cap it, which helps meet limited-energy requirements such as IEC61010-1 and UL1310. A resistor from PLIM to GND sets the limit; PLIM tied to GND turns it off. In an over-power event the TPS26632 holds VOUT × IOUT at the set value for at most tCL_PLIM(dly), 162 ms typical, then MODE decides. TPS26633, TPS26635, TPS26636 and TPS26637 first allow up to VOUT × 2 × IOL for tCB(dly), then limit to the PLIM value.
IMON sources a current proportional to the IN-to-OUT current; a resistor to GND turns it into a voltage, usable up to 4 V. No bypass capacitor goes on IMON, so that the reading is not delayed.

FLT is open drain and goes low on undervoltage, overvoltage, overload, power limiting, reverse current, an ILIM pin short and thermal shutdown. Fault reports are deglitched internally. Unused, FLT may be left open or grounded.

Above T(TSD), 165 °C typical, the FET turns off and FLT goes low. In auto-retry mode the device restarts t(TSD_retry), 648 ms typical, after the junction cools 11 °C below T(TSD); in latch mode it stays off.

Pulling SHDN below 0.8 V turns off both the internal and external FETs and drops the supply current to 21 µA typical; the pull-down must sink at least 10 µA. SHDN at 2 V or more enables the device, which then ramps the output in dVdT mode. It can be driven by a microcontroller GPIO or an opto-isolator.
At least 0.1 µF goes across IN_SYS and GND. None of the IN and OUT pins may be left unconnected.

With ±500 V, 2 Ω surge an SMC TVS such as SMCJ36CA clamps near ±55 V; on a negative strike Q1 sees -(55 V + 24 V) = -79 V, so Q1 is rated at least 80 V and chosen for its RDSON at a 10 V to 14 V gate drive. CSD19537Q3 and BSS138 serve as Q1 and Q2. The PGOOD pull-up is 10 kΩ to 100 kΩ and its sink current stays under 10 mA. CIN is at least 1 µF, which limits slew rates during surge. Grounding OVP and UVLO instead gives the internal defaults, V(OV) = 34.2 V and V(UV) = 15.6 V.

The supply is 4.5 V to 60 V and rated above the set current limit. With the source more than a few inches away, an input ceramic capacitor above 0.1 µF is used. Interrupting current makes input inductance spike the input positive and output inductance spike the output negative, possibly past the absolute maximum ratings. Remedies: short leads, a large GND plane, a Schottky from OUT to GND, a small ceramic input capacitor near 0.1 µF, and a TVS where surge tests apply, with at least 1 µF at the input.

A 0.1 µF or larger ceramic capacitor sits between IN_SYS and GND, as close to those pins as possible with a small loop. Q1's drain sits close to the IN pins on a plane; Q2's drain and source sit very close to Q1's gate and source in a short loop. Power paths are short and sized for at least twice full-load current. RILIM, CdVdT, RIMON and the UVLO, OVP and PGTH resistors sit near their pins with short returns to GND; the RILIM traces are as short as possible and kept away from switching signals. TVS, snubbers and output Schottky sit close to the pins they protect. The PowerPAD is soldered to the GND plane under the device; other layers can add heat sinking.
